requirements.label: Trip, terminal, and timing context

question_templates.terminal_id: Which terminal is this trip going to?
question_templates.trip_at: What date and time is the trip planned for, including the time zone?

limits: These facts select assessment scope; they do not establish dispatch, route, or entry clearance.

The catalog's terminal-specific evidence supports APM Elizabeth only. A missing terminal leaves applicability unresolved, and another terminal creates an unsupported-terminal coverage gap rather than an exemption.
The NJPASS-hosted route-review clause is retained evidence, but its official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

requirements.label: Gross, axle, and spacing evidence

question_templates.gross_weight: What is the loaded gross weight, including the unit?
question_templates.axle_layout: What is the weight on each individual axle and its position measured from the first axle, including units? Leave unknown if only group totals are available.
question_templates.axle_weights: What is the loaded weight on each axle or axle group, including the unit?
question_templates.axle_spacings: What are the axle spacings, including the unit?
question_templates.axle_count: How many axles does the tractor-trailer combination have?
question_templates.route_id: What exact route is planned for this trip?

limits: The federal clause is limited to the Interstate system and reasonable access; the New Jersey single-axle clause is limited to non-Interstate New Jersey roads.
Which limit applies depends on the exact roadway jurisdiction and route. This catalog implements no bridge-formula, axle-group, tire-load, or legal-weight calculator.
Gross weight, axle count, and reported axle weights or spacings do not by themselves establish compliance.
An explicit individual axle layout resolves input structure only. Its sum and span do not execute bridge rules or verify the scale record; legacy arrays remain ambiguous reports.
The NJPASS-hosted route-review clause is excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

requirements.label: Loaded dimensions and exact route access

question_templates.width: What is the loaded overall width, including the unit?
question_templates.height: What is the loaded overall height, including the unit?
question_templates.overall_length: What is the loaded overall vehicle length, including the unit?
question_templates.semitrailer_length: What is the semitrailer length, including the unit?
question_templates.route_id: What exact route is planned for this trip?
question_templates.route_description: Please list the planned roads and terminal-access sequence in travel order.
question_templates.terminal_id: Which terminal is this route intended to access?

limits: Width limits depend on route-network status, and the cited local-access rule is expressly limited to a 102-inch-wide standard truck using unrestricted local roads by the direct route.
A road's absence from a listed network or restriction table establishes neither permission nor prohibition. Current local postings and every segment still require verification.
Published terminal directions and stored route topology are not legal route designation, bridge-clearance evidence, or navigable truck-route approval.

requirements.label: Permit type and load eligibility evidence

question_templates.permit_type: What permit type, if any, is reported for this specific truck and load?
question_templates.container_sealed: Is the container sealed, unknown, or not a sealed container?
question_templates.load_divisible: Is the load divisible, non-divisible, or still unknown?
question_templates.trip_at: What date and time is the permitted movement planned for, including the time zone?
question_templates.permit_route_reported: Does the reported permit identify this exact route and trip?

limits: Permit applicability depends on the load, dimensions, axle facts, trip time, and permit terms; no legal interpretation or permit-validity check is implemented.
The ocean-container sources concern sealed ocean-borne containers and do not make every container move eligible for that permit type.
The NJPASS-hosted permit clause is retained but excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently archived and compared.
A reported permit, including a reported-valid permit, is user-reported evidence and does not establish approval or route coverage.

requirements.label: Cross-authority route and permit coverage

question_templates.route_id: What exact route is planned for this trip?
question_templates.route_description: Which State, toll, county, local, Port Authority, and terminal roads will the move use?
question_templates.permit_route_reported: Does the reported permit identify this exact route and trip?
question_templates.turnpike_approval_reported: Is separate approval from the toll-road authority reported for this route?
question_templates.local_approval_reported: Are the required county or local approvals reported for every local segment?
question_templates.port_approval_reported: Is Port Authority approval reported for this movement?
question_templates.terminal_approval_reported: Is terminal handling approval reported for this movement?

limits: A New Jersey State permit does not establish approval for toll, county, local, Port Authority, or terminal-controlled segments.
The retained Turnpike and marine-terminal clauses concern separate authorities and scopes; their inclusion does not establish that every approval applies to this trip.
Every reported approval requires verification from the responsible authority; a complete set of user reports is not cross-authority clearance.
The retained toll-road approval clause is excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

requirements.label: Current route postings and operating conditions

question_templates.trip_at: What date and time is the trip planned for, including the time zone?
question_templates.route_id: What exact route needs a current-condition check?
question_templates.route_description: Please list the planned roads in travel order so each segment can be rechecked.
question_templates.port_street_in_route: Does the planned route use Port Street?
question_templates.route_conditions_checked_at: When were current postings, closures, lanes, detours, escorts, and restrictions last checked with the responsible authorities?

limits: No live current-policy, posting, closure, lane, detour, escort, or route-condition integration is implemented.
The archived Port Street bulletin is a quarantined dated observation, not a source clause or proof of conditions on the trip date; it must be rechecked before operational use.
A user-reported check time does not verify the result, authority, route coverage, or continued currentness of that check.

requirements.label: DTR registration and vehicle RFID evidence

question_templates.vehicle_id: Which synthetic truck is assigned to this move?
question_templates.dtr_reported: Is this truck reported as currently registered in the DTR?
question_templates.rfid_reported: Is a valid, properly mounted RFID tag reported for this truck?

limits: No live PortTruckPass, DTR, ownership-amendment, or RFID lookup is implemented.
Reported DTR or RFID status is not registry verification and does not establish terminal entry.

requirements.label: DTR engine-policy evidence and retained tariff conflict

question_templates.vehicle_id: Which synthetic truck is assigned to this move?
question_templates.engine_model_year: What is the truck engine model year?
question_templates.dtr_reported: Can an active DTR record for this truck be verified?
question_templates.trip_at: What date and time is terminal entry planned for, including the time zone?

limits: The release preserves an unresolved internal tension between Subrules 34-1101 and 34-1140; the deadline clause is explicitly excluded from verified use.
This catalog does not reconcile the tariff, infer enforcement, or categorically approve or deny a truck from engine model year alone.
The 2014 engine language concerns completing DTR registration and must not be silently converted into a universal terminal-entry rule.

requirements.label: Driver TWIC evidence

question_templates.driver_id: Which synthetic driver is assigned to this move?
question_templates.twic_reported: Does the assigned driver report a current TWIC for the intended access?

limits: The federal clause concerns unescorted access to regulated secure areas and retains its stated exceptions; this catalog does not determine whether an exception applies.
No live TSA or Port Authority credential verification is implemented. A reported TWIC is not verified access authorization.

requirements.label: SeaLink and TWIC registration evidence

question_templates.driver_id: Which synthetic driver is assigned to this move?
question_templates.current_sealink_id: What synthetic SeaLink alias is current for that driver?
question_templates.sealink_registered_reported: Is the driver's current SeaLink reported as active with the TWIC registered to it?
question_templates.twic_reported: Does the assigned driver report a current TWIC for the intended access?

limits: No live SeaLink or TWIC-registration lookup is implemented.
Possession of an identifier and a reported registration do not establish current validity or terminal entry.

requirements.label: APM safety induction tied to the current SeaLink

question_templates.terminal_id: Is this trip going to APM Elizabeth?
question_templates.subject_role: Is the assessed person the truck driver for this move?
question_templates.driver_id: Which synthetic driver is assigned to this move?
question_templates.current_sealink_id: What synthetic SeaLink alias is current for that driver?
question_templates.trip_at: What date and time is terminal entry planned for, including the time zone?
question_templates.induction_reported: Does the driver report completing APM's induction for that current SeaLink?

limits: This is the only catalog requirement with an implemented check, and it uses server-owned synthetic evidence rather than a live training provider.
A matching synthetic result addresses only induction for the current SeaLink; it is not dispatch, route, permit, or terminal-entry clearance.
Archived policy is not verified as current for the trip, and synthetic assessment dates do not create a training-expiry rule.

requirements.label: APM gate appointment evidence

question_templates.terminal_id: Is this gate move going to APM Elizabeth?
question_templates.appointment_reported: Is an appointment reported for this specific APM gate move?

limits: No live TERMPoint or terminal appointment lookup is implemented.
A reported appointment does not establish that it is current, matches this movement, or will be accepted at the gate.

requirements.label: Same-day transaction and gate release evidence

question_templates.terminal_id: Which terminal must release this transaction?
question_templates.trip_at: What date and time is the intended gate move, including the time zone?
question_templates.transaction_release_reported: Is this specific transaction reported as released for the intended gate move?

limits: The pinned release contains no retained source clause that establishes same-day transaction or gate-release requirements.
No live terminal transaction, gate, cargo-release, or admission integration is implemented. Reported release status cannot establish entry.

checks.title: Loaded height and the archived NJ baseline
checks.context: The retained NJ guide states 13 ft 6 in, including the load, except as otherwise identified. Exact roadway applicability, current postings, permit terms and exceptions have not been determined.
checks.next_action: Confirm the loaded height and resolve the exact route, applicable exceptions and oversize authorization with the carrier and road authorities.

checks.title: Loaded width and the 102-inch NJ baseline
checks.context: The retained guide describes 102 inches and a separate 96-inch road category. This comparison does not select either category for the trip. Exact roadway applicability, current postings, permit terms and exceptions have not been determined.
checks.next_action: Verify the loaded width, roadway network classification, local restrictions and any required oversize authorization.

checks.title: Loaded width and the separate 96-inch NJ baseline
checks.context: This is the guide’s separate 96-inch road category. The exact route may belong to another category; route names alone do not decide that. Exact roadway applicability, current postings, permit terms and exceptions have not been determined.
checks.next_action: Verify the loaded width, roadway network classification, local restrictions and any required oversize authorization.

checks.title: Semitrailer length and the archived 53-foot baseline
checks.context: The retained 53-foot text concerns one motor-drawn semitrailer and its power unit. Configuration and exceptions are not evaluated. Exact roadway applicability, current postings, permit terms and exceptions have not been determined.
checks.next_action: Confirm the semitrailer configuration and length, route access rules and any separate authorization.

checks.title: Semitrailer length and the 48-foot access trigger
checks.context: Exceeding 48 feet is an access-review trigger for the cited greater-than-48-through-53-foot category, not a general prohibition. Longer trailers still require separate review.
checks.next_action: Verify the applicable network and any qualifying direct terminal or service access; a listed route or shortest path is not itself access permission.

checks.title: Gross weight and the archived federal baseline
checks.context: The cited 80,000-pound provision concerns Interstate highways and reasonable access, and expressly allows a lower bridge-formula limit. Jurisdiction, permits and exceptions are unresolved.
checks.next_action: Verify the roadway regime, individual axle and axle-group weights, spacings and applicable bridge/permit limits; gross weight alone cannot establish weight compliance.

checks.title: Gross weight and the archived NJ guide baseline
checks.context: The guide describes a standard 80,000-pound overall limit and warns that the bridge formula can require less. Exact applicability and exceptions are unresolved.
checks.next_action: Verify the roadway regime, individual axle and axle-group weights, spacings and applicable bridge/permit limits; gross weight alone cannot establish weight compliance.

checks.title: Reported ocean-container permit and its archived gross limit
checks.context: The retained Table 5 transcription states 90,000 pounds for the described sealed ocean-borne container permit. Legal dimensions, axle groups, ocean-container eligibility and permit validity are separate conditions.
checks.next_action: Resolve any gross-weight excess with the issuer and independently check sealed ocean-container eligibility, legal dimensions, axle groups and actual permit terms.

checks.title: Height and the separate marine-terminal approval trigger
checks.context: The retained terminal tariff calls vehicles over 16 ft 3 in over dimensional. This separate terminal provision does not replace lower roadway limits or other gate requirements.
checks.next_action: Verify whether the terminal provision applies and obtain the relevant marine-terminal handling approval when required; separately resolve roadway height limits.

checks.title: Width and the separate marine-terminal approval trigger
checks.context: The retained terminal tariff calls vehicles over 11 ft wide over dimensional. This separate terminal provision does not replace roadway limits.
checks.next_action: Verify whether the terminal provision applies and obtain the relevant marine-terminal handling approval when required; separately resolve roadway width limits.

checks.title: Gross weight and the containerized-shipment terminal ceiling
checks.context: The 128,000-pound tariff ceiling is for containerized shipments and also requires manufacturer safe working loads. Container applicability and working-load ratings are not established by this comparison.
checks.next_action: Verify containerized-shipment applicability and manufacturer working loads with the terminal; resolve the separate roadway weight and permit requirements.

checks.title: Sealed-container prerequisite in the reported permit category
checks.context: The cited permit description concerns sealed containers used in international ocean-going commerce. A sealed report alone does not establish ocean-borne eligibility.
checks.next_action: Resolve the reported seal status and verify container type, movement eligibility and permit terms with the issuer.

checks.title: Load divisibility in the reported single-trip permit category
checks.context: The retained single-trip permit description concerns a non-divisible load. This check does not decide whether a different authorization or exception exists.
checks.next_action: Resolve the reported load divisibility with the permit issuer and verify that the actual authorization covers this truck, load, route and time.

checks.title: Reported TWIC availability
checks.context: The federal text concerns unescorted secure-area access and retains exceptions; Port SeaLink conditions are separate.
checks.next_action: Resolve reported TWIC absence or uncertainty and verify the intended access and any applicable exception through an authorized source.

checks.title: Reported SeaLink and TWIC registration
checks.context: The retained Port guide describes SeaLink and TWIC registration. A reported identifier is not proof of active registration.
checks.next_action: Resolve the reported registration status and verify the current driver/SeaLink/TWIC association with the Port Authority.

checks.title: Reported truck registration
checks.context: The retained tariff concerns drayage trucks entering Port Authority terminals and registration before entry.
checks.next_action: Resolve the reported DTR status for the assigned truck through an authorized PortTruckPass/registry source.

checks.title: Reported truck RFID
checks.context: The retained guide concerns Class 8 drayage trucks and a valid, properly mounted tag. Applicability and tag validity remain unverified.
checks.next_action: Resolve the reported RFID status and verify tag validity, mounting and association with the assigned truck.

checks.title: Reported APM gate appointment
checks.context: The retained APM text states that all gate moves require an appointment. Actual move matching, timing and acceptance remain unverified.
checks.next_action: Resolve the reported appointment status through TERMPoint or the terminal for this exact move.

checks.title: Axle and bridge calculation remains unexecuted
checks.context: The retained federal clause introduces the bridge formula but does not retain its equation or complete grouping/exception rules. Intake permits individual axle or axle-group reports, so array entries cannot safely be treated as individual axles.
checks.next_action: Obtain explicitly ordered individual axle loads, group membership and defined spacings; review a complete governing formula and exceptions before calculating axle/bridge eligibility.

checks.title: Separate roadway and terminal approvals remain unresolved
checks.context: A State permit report cannot settle which toll, local, port or terminal authorizations apply. The retained NJTA excerpt has specific vehicle/load cases, not a universal 102-inch permission rule.
checks.next_action: Map each actual route segment to its responsible authority and verify which separate approvals cover the vehicle, load and movement.

checks.title: Current route conditions still need an authoritative check
checks.context: A reported check timestamp is not a verified condition result. The separate Port Street observation, if supplied, is archived operating context and cannot establish current restrictions.
checks.next_action: Verify current restrictions and operating conditions for the exact route and trip time with the responsible road authorities.

checks.title: Engine year alone cannot decide DTR or entry eligibility
checks.context: The archive retains an unresolved tension between the DTR registration language and deadline clause. Engine model year is not an emissions certification or a verified active registry record.
checks.next_action: Obtain the truck’s authorized registry/emissions evidence and have the responsible authority resolve the retained tariff interpretation before an eligibility decision.

checks.title: Transaction release has no retained governing clause
checks.context: The catalog has no retained clause establishing this transaction/gate-release requirement and no live release integration.
checks.next_action: Verify the actual transaction and gate state with the terminal, and obtain the governing requirement before implementing a release evaluator.

(d) The maximum gross weight on tandem axles is 34,000 pounds.

record.label: N.J.A.C. 13:18-1.2 — Requirement of permit (NJPASS-hosted rule copy)
source_text: (a) Except as provided in (c) below, a single-trip permit is required for each one-way trip of an oversize or overweight vehicle that exceeds the dimension or weight provisions of N.J.S.A. 39:3-84.
(b) In the event the vehicle is both oversize and overweight, a single-trip permit will be issued for each one-way trip.

(c) An annual ocean borne containerized cargo multiple-trip permit may be issued for a tractor semitrailer combination engaged in the transportation of sealed containers of the type commonly used for the conveyance of freight transportation in international ocean going commerce as follows:

1. Sealed containers transported under an annual ocean borne containerized cargo multiple-trip permit shall bear the seal of the United States Custom Service, the seal of another governmental agency or the seal of a shipper;

2. The combined gross vehicle weight of any tractor semitrailer combination, including load or content conveying sealed containers, shall not exceed 90,000 pounds. The tractor semitrailer combination per-axle combined weight shall not exceed 38,000 pounds for any one tandem axle unit in any tractor semitrailer combination and shall not exceed 56,400 pounds for any tri-axle trailer configuration. Additionally, vehicles shall conform with the axle limitations in N.J.S.A. 39:3-84 and the maximum tire load limit in N.J.A.C. 13:18-1.10(a)2. Vehicles or combination of vehicles that exceed these weight limits may not use an annual ocean borne containerized cargo multiple-trip permit and shall obtain a single-trip permit as described in (a) above;

source_text: As the diagram above shows, the maximum length of a semitrailer shall not exceed 53 feet when operated as part of a combination of vehicles consisting of one motor-drawn vehicle and a drawing or power unit vehicle.

Semitrailers greater than 48 feet in length but not more than 53 feet in length must be transported using the National Network unless seeking food, fuel, rest, repairs or to reach a terminal by the direct route (that is, the shortest travel distance). Upon completing each trip, the large truck should return to the National Network in a manner consistent with reaching its next terminal. Trips off of the National Network or the New Jersey Access Network onto all other local unrestricted roadways should only be for the purpose of accessing a terminal on those roadways, by the shortest distance.

record.label: NJ Commercial Vehicle Size and Weight Guidebook — 3.1 Single-Trip OS/OW Permit
record.source_text: A single-trip permit allows a carrier to haul a non-divisible load above legal size and/or weight limitations and is valid for a single trip within a period of five days. In the event the one-way trip cannot be completed within the valid life of the single-trip permit due to hazardous road conditions or vehicle breakdown, a one-day extension may be granted provided that the request is made to the DOT before the permit has expired. Permit restrictions are assigned based on requested dimensions and weights.

record.label: SUBRULE 34-1100: REGISTRATION IN DRAYAGE TRUCK REGISTRY (DTR)
record.source_text: All Drayage Trucks seeking entry onto any Port Authority Terminal shall be registered in the DTR prior to the date of entry. Registration in the DTR shall be in electronic format via the PortTruckPass (PTP) website (www.porttruckpass.com). Supporting documentation may be required for verification purposes with regard to registration or amendment.

record.label: SUBRULE 34-290: STATE LEGISLATION — Rules and Regulations Governing Traffic on Highways in Port Authority Air and Marine Terminals
source_text: All persons on any air terminal highway or marine terminal highway must at all times comply with any lawful order, signal or direction by voice or hand of any member of the Port Authority police force. When traffic is controlled by traffic lights, signs or by mechanical or electrical signals, such lights, signs and signals shall be obeyed unless a Port Authority police officer directs otherwise.

Unless otherwise directed, all vehicles on any air terminal highway or marine terminal highway shall at all times stay to the right of the center of the roadway, except in the case of one-way roadways; slow- moving vehicles shall remain as close as possible to the right-hand edge or curb of the roadway; and where a roadway is marked with traffic lanes, vehicles shall not cross markings.

No person shall operate a motor vehicle on an air terminal highway or marine terminal highway unless he is duly authorized to operate such vehicle on State and municipal highways in the State in which such air terminal highway or marine terminal highway is located, or unless he is especially authorized by the Port Authority to operate motor vehicles on such air terminal highway or marine terminal highway. No motor vehicle shall be permitted on any air terminal highway or marine terminal highway unless it is registered in accordance with the provisions of the law of the State in which such air terminal highway or marine terminal highway is located, or unless it is especially authorized by the Port Authority to be operated on such air terminal highway or marine terminal highway.
